result.summary: All four verification points confirmed correct. (1) §2.4 point 1 now states, with source citations verified directly against deps/ecto/lib/ecto/type.ex:1007 (`def trim(type, value) when is_binary(value) and type != :binary, do: String.trim_leading(value)`) and deps/ecto/lib/ecto/changeset.ex (filter_values lambda built at line 774 `trim_values.(type, value) in empty_values`, invoked from cast_field/9 at line 897 via filter_values/5 at line 919 -> filter_values/3 at line 938), that validate_required(:rationale) rejects nil, literal "", and whitespace-only strings such as "   " -- all three collapse to "" (a member of default empty_values) via trim_leading before validate_required/2 runs. This matches exactly what I verified empirically in the prior re-check round. (2) The residual-gap narrowing is precise and correct: an all-whitespace string is entirely 'leading' whitespace, so trim_leading collapses the whole thing to "" (rejected); a string like " x " only has its leading space stripped, leaving "x " (non-empty, accepted) -- the design correctly distinguishes these two cases and no longer conflates them, unlike the version that failed the previous round. (3) The DB CHECK's stated gap (CHECK (rationale <> '') does not trim, so a raw SQL insert of '   ' would pass) and the decision to accept this gap is consistent with §8's scope-discipline table and §4's Multi steps -- no update/delete/bulk-insert path bypassing the changeset is defined or exposed anywhere in this design for either artifact_activation_history or artifact_activation_groups, so the 'no changeset-bypassing writer exists' reasoning holds. (4) A full-document grep for 'rationale|whitespace|trim' found no other section repeating either the round-1 false claim (validate_length rejects whitespace) or the round-2 false claim (validate_required does not reject whitespace-only) -- §10's AC6 traceability row now matches §2.4's corrected claim verbatim in substance. Diff against the prior committed version (git diff HEAD~1) confirms only §2.4 and §10's AC6 row changed in this rework; §2.2, §4.1, §4.2, and §7 (OQ-A/OQ-E/OQ-F content, already passed in recheck1) are byte-identical to the version already verified correct. Design is now unambiguous and fully specified for REQ-203's AC6 and its enforcement layers; no implementation code present in the reviewed sections. Routing to Step 2a ELIXIR-DEV.
